n: Since we are surrounded by such a huge crowd of faithful witnesses — the heroes of chapter 11, pictured like spectators in a stadium — let us throw off every burden and clinging sin and run our race with endurance.

f.g: A great crowd of those who testified by their faithful lives.

n: Keep your eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of our faith. For the joy ahead of Him, He endured the cross, scorning its shame, and now sits at the right hand of God’s throne.

f.g: Pioneer and completer — He began faith’s race and finished it perfectly.

f.w: for the joy that was set before him

n: Think about Him who endured such hostility from sinners, so you won’t grow weary and lose heart.
In your struggle against sin, you haven’t yet resisted to the point of shedding blood, as Jesus and the martyrs did.

f.g: Fought to the point of death.

n: Have you forgotten how scripture encourages you as children? “My son, don’t take the Lord’s discipline lightly or lose heart when He corrects you.”

f.w: despise not thou the chastening of the Lord

n: “For the Lord disciplines the one He loves and corrects every child He accepts.”

f.w: whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth

n: Endure hardship as discipline. God is treating you as His children — what child isn’t corrected by a father?

f.w: God dealeth with you as with sons

n: If you never experienced discipline, which all children receive, you would be like illegitimate children without a caring father, not true sons and daughters.

f.g: Illegitimate children, who often lacked a father’s training and inheritance.

n: We respected our earthly fathers who disciplined us. How much more should we submit to the Father of our spirits and truly live? This verse supports the teaching that God is literally the Father of our spirits.
Our earthly fathers disciplined us briefly as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our true good, so we can share His holiness.
No discipline feels pleasant at the time — it hurts. But later it produces a peaceful harvest of righteousness for those trained by it.
So strengthen your drooping hands and weak knees.

f.w: lift up the hands which hang down

n: Make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame isn’t twisted out of joint but healed instead. Our choices help or hurt weaker members too.
Strive for peace with everyone, and for holiness — without which no one will see the Lord.

f.w: no man shall see the Lord

n: Watch out that no one falls short of God’s grace, and that no bitter root springs up to cause trouble and poison many.

f.w: fail of the grace of God
f.g: Fall short of, come up short.

n: Make sure no one is sexually immoral or irreverent like Esau, who traded his birthright for a single meal.

f.g: Godless, treating the sacred as common.

n: You know that later, when Esau wanted the blessing, he was rejected. He couldn’t undo what he had done, though he sought it with tears.

f.g: No way to change the outcome or reverse his father’s decision.

n: You haven’t come to a mountain that can be touched — Sinai — blazing with fire, gloom, darkness, and storm.

f.w: the mount that might be touched

n: Nor to a trumpet blast and a voice so overwhelming that the people begged not to hear another word.

f.w: entreated that the word should not be spoken to them any more

n: They couldn’t bear the command: “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”

f.w: if so much as a beast touch the mountain

n: The sight was so terrifying that even Moses said, “I am trembling with fear.”
Instead, you have come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to countless thousands of angels in joyful assembly.

You have come to the assembly of the Church of the Firstborn, whose names are written in heaven; to God, the Judge of all; and to the spirits of righteous people made perfect. D&C 76 echoes this language describing celestial heirs.

f.w: spirits of just men made perfect

n: And to Jesus, Mediator of the new covenant, and to His sprinkled blood, which speaks a better word than Abel’s. Abel’s blood cried for justice; Christ’s blood speaks mercy.

f.w: Jesus the mediator of the new covenant

n: Be sure you don’t reject the One who is speaking. If those who refused the warning on earth didn’t escape, we certainly won’t if we turn away from Him who warns from heaven.
His voice shook the earth at Sinai, but now He promises, “Once more I will shake not only the earth but heaven too.”

f.w: Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven

n: “Once more” means that created, shakable things will be removed, so that what cannot be shaken will remain.

f.w: those things which cannot be shaken

n: Since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us be thankful and serve God acceptably with reverence and awe.

f.w: a kingdom which cannot be moved

f.g: Let us be grateful (Greek charis also means thanks).

n: For our God is a consuming fire — holy and purifying.

f.w: our God is a consuming fire
